genZNote: Human-adapted, wine-red on the reverse of the culture plate, and behind more athlete's foot than you'd like to think about.

morphology.size: Hyphae ~2-4 µm wide; microconidia teardrop-shaped, ~2-3 µm
morphology.notes: Produces mostly numerous teardrop-shaped microconidia along the hyphae; smooth-walled, pencil-shaped macroconidia are less common and often sparse

habitat.hostAssociation: Anthropophilic — adapted specifically to humans, spread person-to-person rather than from animals or soil
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Survives on shed skin cells in shared environments (locker rooms, shower floors, shared footwear/towels)
habitat.reservoir: Infected humans; contaminated surfaces and fomites

microscopy.stain: KOH preparation of skin/nail/hair scrapings; lactophenol cotton blue for culture
microscopy.appearance: Septate hyphae in KOH prep of skin scrapings; numerous teardrop-shaped microconidia along hyphae in culture

culture.media: Dermatophyte test medium (DTM), Sabouraud dextrose agar
culture.colonyMorphology: White, cottony surface with a characteristic wine-red to reddish-brown pigment on the reverse of the plate

identificationClues: Wine-red to reddish-brown pigment on the reverse side of the culture plate — a classic identifying feature
Numerous teardrop-shaped microconidia along the hyphae, with sparse macroconidia
KOH preparation of skin/nail scrapings shows septate hyphae directly
The most common cause of chronic dermatophyte infections of skin and nails worldwide

clinicalImportance.transmission: Direct skin-to-skin contact or contact with contaminated fomites (shared towels, shoes, locker room/shower floors)
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: The most common dermatophyte causing chronic, recurrent skin and nail infections worldwide; being anthropophilic, it spreads efficiently in communal/shared-facility settings
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: KOH preparation is a quick office-based way to confirm a dermatophyte infection, while the reddish-brown reverse pigment on culture is the classic confirmatory feature for this specific species

examFacts.importantDisease: Tinea pedis, corporis, cruris, and onychomycosis
examFacts.importantTest: KOH preparation of skin scrapings; culture showing wine-red reverse pigment
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Anthropophilic (human-adapted) with a characteristic wine-red reverse pigment on culture
